title: Incense
lead: Fragrant resin burned before God each morning and evening on the golden altar (Exodus 30:1–10, 34–38). The Bible links its rising smoke with prayer (Psalm 141:2; Luke 1:10; Revelation 5:8; 8:3–4), and it is among the gifts brought to the child Jesus (Matthew 2:11).

sections.b: The gold altar and its holy recipe are set out in Exodus 30. Nadab and Abihu die offering strange fire (Leviticus 10:1–2), and on the Day of Atonement a cloud of incense shields the high priest before the ark (Leviticus 16:12–13). Korah's men are destroyed for offering it, while Aaron's incense stops a plague (Numbers 16:35, 46–48). King Uzziah is struck with skin disease for burning incense in the temple (2 Chronicles 26:16–21). The psalmist asks that his prayer rise like incense (Psalm 141:2), and Malachi foresees a pure offering of incense among the nations (Malachi 1:11). Zechariah is serving at the incense altar when the angel comes (Luke 1:8–11), and in Revelation the incense is the prayers of God's people (Revelation 5:8; 8:3–4).
